/**
* Regular expression pattern to split strings into words for various case conversions
*
* This pattern matches sequences of characters in a string, considering the following cases:
* - Sequences of two or more uppercase letters followed by an uppercase letter and lowercase letters or digits (for acronyms)
* - Sequences of one uppercase letter optionally followed by lowercase letters and digits
* - Single uppercase letters
* - Sequences of digits
* - Emojis and other Unicode characters

* The resulting match can be used to convert camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and other mixed formats into
* a consistent format like snake case. It also supports emojis and other Unicode characters.
*
* @example
* const matches = 'camelCaseHTTPRequest🚀'.match(CASE_SPLIT_PATTERN);
* // matches: ['camel', 'Case', 'HTTP', 'Request', '🚀']
*/
const CASE_SPLIT_PATTERN = /\p{Lu}?\p{Ll}+|[0-9]+|\p{Lu}+(?!\p{Ll})|\p{Emoji_Presentation}|\p{Extended_Pictographic}|\p{L}+/gu;
/**
* Splits `string` into an array of its words, treating spaces and punctuation marks as separators.
*
* @param str The string to inspect.
* @param [pattern] The pattern to match words.
* @returns Returns the words of `string`.

*
* words('Lunedì 18 Set')
* // => ['Lunedì', '18', 'Set']
*/
function words(str) {
	return Array.from(str.match(CASE_SPLIT_PATTERN) ?? []);
}
export { CASE_SPLIT_PATTERN, words };

content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. `src/module.ts` is unchanged and nothing was installed.

| | Bundle (min+gzip) | Own code bytes |
|---|---|---|
| Original (lodash) | 9360 | 164 |
| Migrated | 2009 | 85 |

Type checking passes (`npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`). The four example inputs give the same results as lodash.

What's in the file:

- **`applyPatch`** uses `merge` from `es-toolkit`. It matched lodash on 100k random base/patch pairs that follow the input range.
- **`toTitle`** uses `startCase` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main-entry `startCase` lowercases the rest of each word, so `"HELLO WORLD"` becomes `"Hello World"` instead of lodash's `"HELLO WORLD"`. A `words` + `upperFirst` adapter from the main entry matched on most inputs but split digit boundaries differently (`"Y2nd"`), so I rejected it. The compat version matched on 300k random keys.
- **`toLookup`** uses `fromPairs` from `es-toolkit/compat`. The main entry has no `fromPairs`. A `zipObject` adapter also matched but came out larger (2077 vs 2009 bytes), so I kept compat.

The `Row` and `Config` exports and all three function signatures are unchanged. No lodash import remains.

The equivalence checks were randomized comparisons I ran in the scratchpad, not a formal proof. The merge generator only produces patches that follow the input range.
